notes.title: Forgive Me Father 2 is Out of Early Access Now!
notes.notes:
Greetings, everyone!

Allow us to inform you, loyal players of Lovecraft's Untold Stories, that another comic-style Lovecraftian nightmare from Fulqrum Publishing has just left Early Access and is available now - the game is none other than [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2272250/Forgive_Me_Father_2/]Forgive Me Father 2[/url]!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2272250/Forgive_Me_Father_2/

Drawing inspiration from various FPS subgenres, including classic boomer shooters like Quake and Doom, combined with modern mechanics, unique visual style, and Unreal Engine 5 technology, [b]Forgive Me Father 2 offers an action-packed retro-meets-cutting-edge love letter to all FPS fans[/b]. 

Building upon the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1590910/Forgive_Me_Father/]original[/url] with a darker story, players are now entrenched deeper into the mythos, with equipable [b]Dark Tome[/b] pages to upgrade their madness skills. Be that healing wounds with [b]Lifesteal[/b], becoming more powerful with [b]Might[/b], boosting fire rate and reload speed with [b]Haste[/b], or reducing incoming damage with [b]Resistance[/b], players can give their mind to the eldritch apparitions to improve their chances of survival. 

While Forgive Me Father 2 has seen multiple major updates over its Early Access period, today’s 1.0 launch introduces [b]tons of new content including vast new levels, new weapons, eldritch monstrosities to battle, and much, much more[/b]!

Starting from today, players will be able to explore the suitably-named Nightmare Land, a low-gravity Hellscape filled with gigantic mushrooms, and of course, hordes of Lovecraftian monstrosities ready to devour their flesh and soul. If mushrooms aren’t your thing, why not face the chilly horrors of the new Arctic level, which also launches as part of today’s 1.0 release?

Players will also be able to get their hands on new tools of destruction, such as the melee weapon known as ‘The Suspicious Box’, which clears theirs personal space when surrounded by hideous monstrosities. Or if you’d prefer, why not kill enemies through sight alone? Then you’ll love the latest addition to the Dark Tome system, which wounds enemies within your sight at unbelievable frequency. No one is safe as long as you have a clear line of sight to your target. 

Get Forgive Me Father 2 for a discounted price and if you think playing the second installment without even trying the first one, be informed that there is a bundle that includes both of these games and that offers a bundle discount (this discount applies even if you already own one of the included games).

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/35903/Forgive_Me_Father_Franchise_Bundle/

notes.title: Try Upcoming Fulqrum Publishing Games at Steam Next Fest Now!
notes.notes:
Greetings, everyone!

Steam Next Fest is upon us! With so many titles to choose from this week, it’s easy to get lost. And that’s why [url=https://store.steampowered.com/developer/FulqrumPublishing/]Fulqrum Publishing[/url] is on hand, with a diverse selection of three demos among which we are certain you can find a new favourite! Will you to take a stand  in the eternal conflict between Arcane Magic and Steampunk Revolution in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2458310/New_Arc_Line/]New Arc Line[/url], prove your political brilliance in a grand strategy that will take your legacy to the stars in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2298690/Realpolitiks_3_Earth_and_Beyond/]Realpolitiks 3: Earth and Beyond[/url], or become a master of sword and magic in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1182420/VED/]VED[/url]? 

[u][b][h3][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2458310/New_Arc_Line/]New Arc Line[/url][/h3]
[/b][/u]
Take a stand in the eternal conflict between Arcane Magic and Steampunk Revolution and tip the uneasy balance between sorcery, elves, dwarves and mysterious monsters on one side and steampunk gadgets, zeppelins, and tesla guns on the other in this single-player, party-based, story-rich RPG.

In the demo, you will be thrown right into the middle of a deadly epidemic of the Iron Plague - select from 2 classes and play as either a Voodoo Shaman or a Diesel Engineer of either the Human or Elven race, and investigate what's going on in the Leprosarium; a hospital specializing in treating patients in the Slums district suffering from the horrific disease. With several ways of completing the quest and moral decisions to make along the way, will you rise to the occasion?

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2458310/New_Arc_Line/


[u][b][h3][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2298690/Realpolitiks_3_Earth_and_Beyond/]Realpolitiks 3: Earth and Beyond[/url][/h3][/b][/u]
Prove your political brilliance in a grand strategy like no other: pick any contemporary country, set up your government and navigate the pitfalls of domestic and international politics. A glorious destiny awaits - the domination of not just the Earth, but the whole Solar system!

The demo will allow you to govern either Germany or Mexico, and you will have 5 in-game years to show off your cunning leadership skills in the new, extreme Overdrive mode. At launch, any contemporary nation will be available for your ambitions, from Afghanistan to Zimbabwe and everything in between, and you will be able to enjoy different campaign modes to boot!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2298690/Realpolitiks_3_Earth_and_Beyond/

VED is a story-driven, hand-drawn RPG with a unique turn-based combat system and roguelite elements. Set in two different worlds, VED tells the story of Cyrus, a young hero who sets out on a quest to become a master of sword and magic, and save everything he knows from destruction.

The demo will let you sneak a peek at a very early part of the game's story - just enough to whet your appetite, but with no significant spoilers!

[h1]News and improvements:[/h1]
[list]
[*] We have added new music tracks that include:

[list]
[*] 2 new ambience tracks for the game's levels.
[*] 4 reactive looped tracks for combat situations.
[*] Game over track song.
[*] Victory track song, while facing a Great Old One.
[*] Defeat track song, while facing a Great Old One.  
[/list]

[*] Final balance of the Thief: This was a tricky one. We have focused mainly on the difficult progression between levels. The main problem that we saw with the Thief was that in the first levels, she was really weak, and had a lot of survival issues but, once got geared, became a melee tank, losing every part of the stealthy theory behind this character, that we wanted to keep.

[list]
[*] We have added a "Bleeding effect" to the basic attack of the Thief.
[*] Bugs and Tentacles traps won´t react if you activate Stealth.
[*] We have reworked the HP & range of the enemies, as well as their behaviour to match the "melee" condition of our character. Still, you will face plenty of range enemies, and you should kill them as quick as you can.
[*] We have added the possibility of "cancelling" the attack of the Thief by moving in the opposite direction to where she is facing. Why this? Because before the character was kind of stuck in the attack animation, and would receive a lot of damage.
[*] We have increased a lot the damage of the throwing knives. They should play now an important part of the strategy. Also, we have lowered their price in the shop.
[/list]

We are very happy with the final result and, even though the Thief well geared is still a killing machine, the stealthy approach shall be needed most of the time. No more tanking around!
[/list]

notes.title: Lovecraft's Untold Stories and its giant penguins get a release date
notes.notes:
You can’t walk down the street without tripping over some kind of eldritch horror these days, so Lovecraft’s Untold Stories has an uphill struggle convincing me that there’s anything left to say about the Cthulhu mythos. After a stint in Early Access, the action roguelike is launching on January 31. Check out the official trailer above. 

In a previous life as a freelancer, I reviewed the Early Access version of Lovecraft’s Untold Stories, and the one thing that’s stuck with me is the penguins. The objectively best birds aren’t the sort of critters you might expect in a Lovecraft game, but they’re all over the place in the chilly final level. 

We’re not talking regular penguins, either. These are the massive albino penguins from At the Mountains of Madness, and while they never attacked me during my journey through these apparently Untold Stories, they did freak me out quite a lot with their horrific screams. Horrific, human screams. Awful stuff. 

I’ve never been so afraid of penguins before, so I guess that’s one mark in Untold Stories’ favour, though the Early Access version was pretty bare bones and, despite the name, largely mining the same Lovecraft yarns we’ve seen countless times already. 

Check out our list if you fancy some horror universes that have nothing to do with Lovecraft.

notes.title: Introducing Elizabeth des Flèches, the Witch
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32875664/932943d5e2d838a030ec54525ca1d7eb8f629264.png[/img]

Greetings, investigators,

Do not worry: we have performed the rituals to keep the dark forces at bay; there won’t be any unintended visitors today. 

We’ve got good news for a change, and we wouldn’t want anyone interrupting. What could possibly constitute good news when we’re facing crawling horrors as ancient and powerful as the forces of creation? Nothing less than a new ally to fight them. We are aware that we can’t win for good – but maybe with her help we can postpone our defeat and forestall the plans of the Great Old Ones one more day…

Let us introduce you to [b]the witch Elizabeth des Flèches[/b]. She was born in southern France, but her mother was wise enough to raise her in the old ways, following the ancient trails to the ruins of the Druidic temples. She learnt forgotten sorceries, and in her trances and visions she discovered the malignant creatures that threaten the very fabric of our world, always lurking our existence at the distance of a mere shadow.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32875664/0b31f3426316d4f062ed2b381f7c7adbeec76577.gif[/img]

In one of her sulfur-induced dreams, she saw sacred stone circles, now corrupted on the top of unknown mountains; stone pillars, silent guardians of the eternal sleep of the faithful, turned to dark purposes. And when she woke up, there were strange prints all around them, like the claws of monstrous birds, and a new power had been bestowed upon her: she could make lighting shoot from her fingertips; the elements played and danced for her, becoming her shield… and her sword.

[b]The Witch[/b] is the third character available in [i]Lovecraft’s Untold Stories[/i]. A fast-moving character, Elizabeth has an above-average knowledge of the Cthulhu Mythos thanks to her training as a sorcerer. She attacks from mid-range using his skull as a magic focus, as well as using the elements to create varied effects, defensive as well as offensive. The Witch joins the Detective and the Professor in a diverse ensemble of characters, each with a very different pace and gameplay features.

Our time is running out. Soon this place will not be safe. The Witch will contact you, investigators. For now, you must depart.

Good luck out there.

[i]The Devs[/i]

notes.title: Lovecraft's Untold Stories Lore (Part 2) - Innsmouth
notes.notes:
Welcome, investigators. Hurry up, come in: we’ve got information that it will prove useful in your struggle against the cosmic horrors… but beware, for it could be your undoing too if you don’t use this information wisely and carefully.  We’ve heard about an accursed place with special significance for the creatures of the Cthulhu Mythos: a town called [b]Innsmouth[/b], in Massachusetts, a horrendous place where, apparently, the vilest of deeds take place.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32875664/a85f275573add58501fab82299239b0e57de083a.jpg[/img]

Innsmouth was invented (or maybe discovered, who knows?) by H.P. Lovecraft, and first referenced in 1920 in Celephaïs as a village in England. However, the most famous incarnation of this place is the one you can read in [i]The Shadow over Innsmouth[/i], published in Weird Tales in 1936 – this time placed in Massachusetts, USA. Innsmouth is a cursed village, a place in a terrible state of decay, so rotten that looks like about to collapse on itself.

This sea town had a sinister history behind it, with hundreds of people disappearing over the years, rumors of dark cults ongoing, and rampant interbreeding that led to madness and deformities. Its inhabitants, a silent people with strange bulging eyes, hide a terrible secret: after a dark pact made in the past by a greedy sailor, for centuries they have mated with the Deep Ones, monsters of the sea and servants of the Old Ones, in exchange for power and riches.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32875664/94968a5a39007ba411d6e2f8d15c88cd111fec44.png[/img]

In his fight against the creeping horrors that threaten to devour our world, the Detective will end up finding and exploring the town of Innsmouth. There, he will meet some new terrible enemies, such as the [b]lurkers[/b] (half-breed of humans and Deep Ones), members of the Esoteric Order of Dagon (a dark religious cult that worship [b]Father Dagon[/b], a powerful Old One who dwells in the darkest bottoms of the oceans) – and who knows what other dangers live in this accursed town... Therein Innsmouth, the Detective has to find something that he needs to face the Old Ones for the first time – but Innsmouth does not give up its secrets easily…

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32875664/1f0c807e7a9741381c25ecc8c47737161d2fcef5.gif[/img]

Innsmouth will be included as a new level in next major update of [i]Lovecraft’s Untold Stories[/i], [u]to be released this weekend[/u], expanding the world of the game and its narrative, and digging deeper in Lovecraft’s work. Prepare for the next step in your eternal fight against the cosmic horrors, investigators. We hope this information proves useful to you. Leave now, before They detect you here and find out that you learned more about their hideouts and plans. 

Good luck, investigators. We hope to see you again.

[i]The Devs[/i]

notes.title: Lovecraft's Untold Stories Lore (Part 1) - The Hospital
notes.notes:
Greetings, investigators! The stars are favorable tonight, and the dark powers we fight against are silent. That means that we have some time to talk, and we’d like to go deeper into the Hospital, one of the levels currently available in [i]Lovecraft’s Untold Stories[/i], to explain where its inspiration came from. 

Hospitals are a common place in horror stories – we relate them with sickness, pain, and death, and that scares everyone for obvious reasons. But the Hospital in Lovecraft’s Untold Stories is not a random, run-of-the-mill scary location. It’s directly inspired by a Lovecraft short story, one with its own place in the history of the genre: [i]Herbert West—Reanimator[/i], serialized first in an amateur magazine and published some time later in the pulp classic magazine [i]Weird Tales[/i].

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32875664/7e10d7bc67d93441713a5fa3a73c72d154d865f5.jpg[/img]

Although this story was not exactly one of Lovecraft’s favorites, it holds some significance for his later works. For a start, it’s the first mention of Miskatonic University, a fictional place located in Arkham (in turn, a fictional town in Massachussetts). Miskatonic is famous for holding a genuine copy of the Necronomicon; under its surface of a serious, Harvard-like teaching institution, its faculty has an ongoing interest for the occult. Almost 20 characters out of its Faculty appear in different Lovecraft stories playing different roles. They usually try to explain first, and fight later, the appearances of creatures from the Cthulhu Mythos and all the phenomena related to them.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32875664/1d02a46e90642ed4c89c291fa9da6d62f7a9dbe7.gif[/img]

[i]Herber West—Reanimator[/i] is also one of the first depiction of zombies as reanimated corpses with mindless, violent, and cannibalistic impulses. Inspired by (and up to some point, mocking) Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein, Herbert West is a scientist who turns to grave-robber to get corpses for his experiments in reanimating dead bodies using a mysterious serum created by him. This story is more a pulp fiction than Lovecraft’s cosmic horror: mad scientists, brain-eating monsters, gruesome murders, and sinister locations.

The Hospital in the game is a direct reference to [i]Herbert West—Reanimator[/i] that we have mixed with other creatures of the Mythos, creating our own Untold Story.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32875664/2b7f0a8a2935e0748b2f58f4f4ea9e29945e4196.gif[/img]

The Hospital is not the only location directly inspired in Lovecraft’s stories that you will find in [i]Lovecraft’s Untold Stories[/i]. Stay tuned, because next week we’ll introduce you to another one: the infamous Innsmouth, found in stories such as [i]The Shadow Over Innsmouth[/i].

Until then, we hope you have good luck in your struggle against the Mythos, investigators – you’re going to need it for sure… 

See you next week!

[i]The devs[/i]

notes.title: Premature Evaluation: Lovecraft s Untold Stories
notes.notes:
Premature Evaluation is the weekly column in which we explore the wilds of early access. This week, Fraser s investigating eldritch goings on in action-RPG Lovecraft s Untold Stories. Never heard of him.

Just when I thought Lovecraft had been mined to death, Lovecraft s Untold Stories comes along and I find myself protecting giant penguins and blowing up pink blobs of toxic goo. You remember the giant penguins from At the Mountains of Madness, don t you? Of course you do! They re the best bit, though tragically underutilised. By giving them their time in the spotlight, Lovecraft s Untold Stories fulfils its titular promise.

It begins rather conventionally, though: a note from a mentor, a spooky mansion, a cult up to no good. For a single level, it toes the line, cramming in all the familiar tropes. Then it starts throwing in gun-toting space bugs. It s kinda Lovecrafty (I m over Lovecraftian), just like it s kinda an RPG and kinda a roguelike.

notes.title: About character progression, balancing & control system
notes.notes:
[h1]CHARACTER PROGRESSION[/h1]

Welcome, investigators. Fighting cosmic horrors is hard enough for us to try to make it even more challenging. [b]That is why Lovecraft’s Untold Stories uses a save and character progression system[/b] – a feature that makes the game stand out from an important part of the roguelike crowd.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32875664/bab4b23faab0c5287e132f9e3bc0b3d26416d2bc.png[/img]

When you beat a level, you can visit the Strange Place: a special room created by the powerful and technologically advanced Great Race of Yith. Thanks to their technology, you can keep the items you find in your adventures in this place between dimensions. After your character dies, you can visit the Strange Place to claim back your “treasure”; you can even share items between characters. For instance, if the Detective finds an item that only Dr. Clawstone can use, like mines, he can leave them in a chest for the professor.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32875664/27f9bcb7f432044df0b86fc10d9c0d055e8407f8.png[/img]

We implemented another helpful feature. [b]You can hit Restart after you die, and instead of going back to the very start of your adventure, you only have to start the same level – with the items that you had when you entered it for the first time[/b]. 

[h1]BALANCING[/h1]

We do know that Lovecraft’s Untold Stories is a difficult game that puts your skills to a test… but, well, no one said that fighting the Old Ones would be easy! Even so, [b]we are paying close attention to your feedback, and we are working as hard as we can to find the right balance in difficulty and progression following your advice[/b].

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32875664/32f134a6a24b291a25db70e07efc46e774dfcd12.png[/img]

[h1]CONTROLS[/h1]

This is another hot topic of discussion in the community: the control scheme. Right now, Lovecraft’s Untold Stories supports gamepad and customizable keyboard. [b]Some of you have asked us to implement mouse + keyboard[/b], and not feeling like this no more...

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32875664/ed2b1d1c8ee45e31588fcb5731020415f3d49b8f.gif[/img]

We are discussing and considering this request; at this point, we can only say that, [b]for next July’s major update (oh, did you know that there will be a big update on July?) we will sit down to discuss it, invoke Nodens to ask for his advice, and see if (and how) we can make it happen[/b]. We’ll keep you posted.

That’s all for today, investigators. Thanks for coming, and mind your own shadows – we’ve heard disturbing reports… but that’s not something we can discuss here and now. See you soon!

notes.title: Introducing Dr. Clawstone
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32875664/a6d512de6448a387a11a0585bfc45bcb6ccedf54.jpg[/img]

Welcome, investigators. Please close the door behind you – strange things are howling in the wind tonight. Today we want to introduce you to Dr. Clawstone, another ally in our endless struggle against the twisted lurking monsters that threaten the very existence of our world. [b]Dr. Clawstone used to do… let’s say, unorthodox research for the American army.[/b] After unearthing a mysterious artifact of unknown origins that he dubs “Tillinghast,” Dr. Clawstone discovered a new type of energy fields that could affect biological organisms.  

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32875664/aa45d1acaf8f4113241dd5c257518b03042778c5.gif[/img]

The Tillinghast proved to be useful when strange bubbling creatures started to leak through the walls of Dr. Clawstone’s library. [b]He could destroy those abnormalities using the artifact, now turned into a weapon.[/b] The veil that blinds humanity in blissful ignorance lifted that day for Clawstone. And when he heard of sightings of energy fields similar to the ones created with the Tillinghast, he decided that he could not stand idle anymore while the Earth is in such grave danger.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32875664/d4f9576d8b95f37e0f730b3ae237d384530f27d3.gif[/img]

Dr. Clawstone’s Tillinghast is basically a means to contain a strange type of energy. It allows him to liberate this energy in quick bursts, equivalent to the shot of a weapon for all purposes. [b]These bursts can hurt all the creatures of the Myths;[/b] we estimate that it might be a type of energy from their own dimensions, hence its ability to hurt them. Dr. Clawstone can also release this energy in a controlled manner to create [b]a protective barrier around his body.[/b] This barrier protects him while causing damage to anything in direct contact with it – although by some unknown mechanisms it draws from Clawstone’s stamina. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32875664/97b531ae0b3a67e42543d05f8bc9bd5c66c9ba18.gif[/img]

[b]Dr. Clawstone joins the Detective as the second character available in Lovecraft’s Untold Stories,[/b] the action RPG with roguelike elements that releases tomorrow (June 22) on Steam Early Access. notes.title: New Creatures

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32875664/5fb970572548b6f265ab5a44d20bf363d037d246.jpg[/img]

Welcome, investigators. Today we want to share with you information that has come to our hands [b]about some of the foul aberrations that we’re facing.[/b] Please be careful with it: we understand that knowledge is vital if we want a chance against these creatures, but it could drive to madness weaker minds than yours.  

[h1]MI-GO, THE FUNGI FROM YUGGOTH[/h1]

The Mi-Go were discovered to humanity by H.P. Lovecraft in his novella [i]The Whisperer in Darkness[/i]. They are fungus-based lifeforms, apparently native from Yuggoth, a mysterious planet at the very edge of our Solar System that some scholars identify with Pluto. [b]When you face the Mi-Go, take into account that they can fly – and they move really, really fast.[/b] Their weapons are unknown to us, alien technology so advanced that our scientific knowledge cannot even grasp its working. Their heinous appearance is too horrific to be put into words, and they are said to be impossible to film or photograph, because ordinary film cannot capture the otherworldly matter that forms their bodies. However, we have managed to film them nevertheless, so you know beforehand what you are facing.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32875664/7d69fa05bdecc02d08f61f557dfdfadbe9978c1f.gif[/img]

[h1]STAR SPAWN, THE OFFSPRING OF MIGHTY CTHULHU[/h1]

The Star Spawn are the offspring and servants of the Great Old One Cthulhu, who lies dreaming in the sunken city of R’Lyeh. They waged wars eons ago against the Elder Things, and perished or went into slumber along with their lord Cthulhu when R’Lyeh sunk. But some of them still roam the Earth or are brought back by the dark sorcery of mad cultists. [b]They are strong, bulky creatures who favor close combat,[/b] but they can also wield powerful magic if need be. They are octopus-like creatures, just like Mighty Cthulhu, but of less stature and sheer power than their god-king. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32875664/5b69c08cec3babe9686becbd097082e24d3a618f.gif[/img]

notes.title: New Combat Mechanics
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32875664/2976420db157df2d13d621f0a59f8a58f2a20897.jpg[/img]

Welcome, investigators. Do not worry: we are safe from prying eyes here, from those who adore the abhorrent entities who seek to destroy our world. We can talk safely about [b]how we will fight against these foul creatures in Lovecraft’s Untold Stories[/b], the action RPG that will be released on Steam Early Access on June, 22!

With this post, [b]we start a dev blog where we will introduce you to different features, enemies, items,[/b] etc. of the game, as well as explain what we are working in and our development roadmap for the future. We intend to keep updating this dev blog after the game is available on Early Access, so make sure to subscribe to these blogs to stay up to date! [b]Today we want to share with you some changes we are implementing in the combat system[/b] that will be available on June 22: a major overhaul of the shooting mechanic and a brand new explosive weapon.

[h1]INTRODUCING A NEW SHOOTING MECHANIC[/h1]

Up until now, and following the lead of other classic games in the genre, Lovecraft’s Untold Stories featured a 2 axis shooting mechanic. That meant that you could shoot up, down, left, and right, but not diagonally – as you can see in our free demo available here. After lots of testing and careful consideration, [b]we have decided to implement a 4 axis shooting mechanic. Thus, you will be able to shoot diagonally too[/b] – facing the Old Ones and Outer Gods is difficult enough to not shooting them as they come! 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32875664/6c2a018c5a59193f8d9d79fe1e1d9828ca2e95b2.gif[/img]

[h1]INTRODUCING MOLOTOV COCKTAILS[/h1]

The cosmic horrors and their Earthling cultists are tough, and sometimes a bullet (or, well, a lot of bullets) is not enough to stop them. Bringing a knife to a gunfight is never a good idea – [b]but bringing explosives, on the other hand…[/b] 

The Detective, one of the characters of Lovecraft’s Untold Stories, can use explosives in combat against the creatures of the Myths. Until now he could only throw them dynamite sticks; [b]today we introduce Molotov cocktails.[/b] As you know, a Molotov cocktail is a half-improvised weapon: a bottle full of an inflammable liquid (usually some kind of alcohol) with a piece of cloth which acts as a fuse. When thrown they explode on impact, setting everyone in the area of effect on fire.

Weapons consisting of a recipient full of an explosive or inflammable liquid are older than that, but [b]Molotov cocktails got their name in the Winter War, when the USSR invaded Finland in 1939.[/b] These improvised weapons, used mostly by partisans in guerrilla warfare or street resistance, were named sarcastically after Soviet politician Viacheslav Mólotov, who in his radio propaganda said that the USSR planes were dropping food and supplies, and not bombs, over the civilian population. With dry sarcasm, the Finnish started calling Soviet bombs “Mólotov’s baskets,” and their Army countered Mólotov’s propaganda announcing that “if Mólotov puts food in the table, we will take care of the cocktails.” The name stuck, and the rest is (quite bloody) history. 

We are aware that they are a bit of an anachronism: Lovecraft’s stories are based years before the invention of Molotov cocktails. But, well, [b]the Old Ones have strange effects over time itself.[/b] Who knows, what other oddities our heroes may face on their way?
